attribution: Swami Vivekananda; a collection of his lectures
author: vivekananda
period: Lectures given mainly in 1896, largely in London; published as a collection shortly afterwards
summary: Vivekananda's lectures presenting Advaita Vedanta to Western audiences as a rational philosophy of knowledge and freedom.
whyRead: It shows how Advaita was reframed in the modern period for a global audience, in the language of reason, science and universal religion. It is a modern exposition, not a classical text, and reflects Vivekananda's own emphases.

keyTeachings.title: Maya as a statement of fact
keyTeachings.text: Vivekananda presents maya not as a theory that the world is an illusion but as a description of the contradictions in which we live.

keyTeachings.title: The real nature of the human being
keyTeachings.text: The true Self is presented as infinite and free, identical with Brahman, with bondage an apparent limitation.

keyTeachings.title: Religion and reason
keyTeachings.text: He argues that Vedanta can meet the demands of reason and science, and that realisation, not belief, is the core of religion.

relatedTexts.note: A classical text of the path of knowledge in Advaita
